## Summary

Added Japanese localization for the `/login` and `/register` pages using the app's existing (previously unused) i18n framework:

- **`src/app.ts`** — added `'ja'` to `i18n.supported` (was `['en']`), enabling Accept-Language-based locale detection for `ja`/`ja-JP` etc., with `en` remaining the fallback for no/unmatched/lower-priority headers.
- **`lang/en/messages.json`** — added an `auth.login.*` and `auth.register.*` key tree holding the exact English copy that used to be hardcoded in the page components (title, heading, subtitle, field labels, submit button, footer question/link).
- **`lang/ja/messages.json`** (new) — mirrors the same key tree with the Japanese translations from the spec, plus a Japanese `welcome` translation (`:nameへようこそ！`) preserving the `:name` placeholder.
- **`resources/js/pages/auth/Login.tsx`** / **`Register.tsx`** — replaced all hardcoded English strings (including `<Head title>`) with `useTranslation()` / `t('messages.auth.…')` calls, so rendering follows the request-resolved locale automatically.
- **`.guren/translations.gen.ts`** — regenerated via `bun run codegen` (now types 20 keys across `en`/`ja`).
- **`tests/AuthLocale.test.ts`** (new) — exercises `/login` and `/register` with the Inertia JSON protocol to verify locale resolution for a typical Japanese browser header, no header, English-preferred headers, English-outranks-Japanese, and an unsupported-only (`fr-FR`) header, plus confirms both catalogs' wording.

Verified `bunx guren check --i18n` (full key parity for both locales), `bun run typecheck`, and `bun test` (9 pass, 0 fail) all pass.
